newsitem.title: USA: Bulls running strong, but may pause for new data.
newsitem.headline: Bulls running strong, but may pause for new data.

text.p: The bulls ran rampant on Wall Street this week, with the blue-chip Dow index setting record highs every day and posting its biggest weekly gain ever.
But next week's May consumer price report and the so-called triple witching expiration of futures and options could prompt a round of profit-taking.
"There is nothing wrong with this picture," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment strategist at First Albany.

"The economy is slow, interest rates are declining, and earnings estimates are up," he said. "Having cash in a portfolio in a market that's going straight up is a drag on performance, so all the money is going straight into stocks."
On Friday, the Dow Jones industrial average rose 70.57 points to a record 7,782.04 -- its sixth consecutive record. For the week, the index of 30 blue-chip stocks was up 346.26 points.
The stock market has gained 1,000 points in just a little over a month as portfolio managers have ploughed fresh cash in stocks.
According to the Investment Company Institute, money managers put $18.5 billion into stock mutual funds in May, an 18 percent increase from April.
A.C. Moore, chief investment strategist at Principal Financial Securities, sees the Dow going above 8,000 before any significant correction, based on current cash flows.

The Dow's latest move upward came Friday on the heels of a larger-than-expected drop in May wholesale prices. The Producer Price Index added to investor euphoria that had been sparked a day earlier by news of a slight drop in May retail sales.
Analysts are expecting Tuesday's release of May consumer prices to reinforce the optimism.

"Based on the Producer Price Index the Consumer Price Index should be more of the same thing we have -- an economy which is slowing and there's very little sign of upward pressure on prices," First Albany's Johnson said.
"It's not insanity," Moore said of the record-breaking run. "It's based on a slowing economy and better earnings predictions."
Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter, said he saw the present trends continuing through the month.

"Theres a strong upward bias until the end of quarter," he said. "We have a declining bond yield, the retail numbers were kind of flat. That may continue," Canelo said. "My guess is that we should see some top next quarter."
The Dow will likely meet some turbulence around Friday's "triple-witching" expirations of stock index futures and options and options on individual stocks.

"You will see a lot of volume but most of the volatility on Thursday," said Doug Myers of Interstate/Johnson Lane. But he said stocks would likely move higher on Friday's activity. "It just keeps going up," he said.
Ralph Bloch, chief technical analyst at Raymond James and Associates, said he's wary of triple witching strategies.
"When the Dow stands perpendicular it's out for a bout of profit-taking. People are using strength for buying ... and from time to time you are supposed to use strength for selling," he said.
"I'm not the genie in the bottle, but there's a saying that 'Bulls make money, bears make money and pigs get slaughtered.' It's too long to believe in the tooth fairy," Bloch said.
For the week, the Nasdaq composite index gained 18.2 points to 1,423.04, the Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 35.26 points to 893.27, and the American Stock Exchange index added 15.45.
